claims.text: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese confirmed that 34 Australians were missing in Nepal following flash floods.
Flash floods occurred at Trishuli in Nuwakot district, Nepal, on August 26, 2026.
At least 57 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu were among the Indians stranded in Nepal during the flash floods on August 26, 2026.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay ordered coordinated rescue efforts and directed Tamil Nadu House in New Delhi to assist stranded pilgrims in Nepal.
The Tamil Nadu state government set up round-the-clock toll-free helpline numbers for family members of stranded tourists.
The 57 stranded pilgrims from Tamil Nadu went to Nepal on a tour organized by a Kumbakonam-based company partnered with a Nepal-based firm.
About 21 pilgrims managed to find shelter at a Nepal border police outpost during the flood.
Isha Foundation founder Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev stated on August 26, 2026, that 495 people from their tour returned safely, 743 were in Tibet, and 148 were in Nepal.
The Rasuwagadhi Himalayan corridor has served for more than 260 years as a major trans-Himalayan trade route between Nepal and Tibet.
More than 6,500 Chinese electric vehicles entered Nepal through the Rasuwagadhi crossing in 2025-26.
Hundreds of 40-foot shipping containers parked along the Timure riverbanks were dislodged and swept downstream by floodwaters.
The flash flood destroyed Miteri Sanghu, also known as Friendship Bridge, across the Lhende/Koshi river at the Nepal-China border.
Survivors of flash flooding in Nepal described the moment their homes were swept away in a landslide.
A 32-member tour group from Kolkata was untraceable following the floods in Nepal.
India and China jointly announced an eight-point consensus following special representatives talks co-chaired by Ajit Doval and Wang Yi in Beijing.
India and China agreed to establish two additional military meeting points and two new channels of border military hotlines.
India and China agreed to hold the 26th round of special representatives talks in India in 2027.
India is scheduled to host the BRICS Summit on September 12, 2026.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping previously met in October 2024 and during 2025 in Tianjin.
The Special Representatives mechanism was established in 2003 to finalize a framework for resolving the 3,488-km India-China border dispute.
India expressed appreciation for Chinese efforts to increase the number of batches for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra pilgrimage.
India and China agreed to reopen three designated border trading points.
China is constructing a $137-billion mega dam on the upper reaches of the Brahmaputra river on the Tibetan plateau.
Indian National Security Adviser Ajit Doval met Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng prior to delegation talks in Beijing.
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi invoked the phrase 'Dragon-Elephant Dance' to describe cooperation between India and China despite differences.
A violent military clash in Galwan Valley in June 2020 resulted in the deaths of 20 Indian soldiers and four Chinese soldiers.
In October 2024, India and China agreed on a patrolling arrangement along the Line of Actual Control that led to troop disengagement in eastern Ladakh.

Supreme Court judge Justice Sandeep Mehta sent three letters in August 2026 to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant alleging misconduct by Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma.
Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma was appointed Acting Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court in September 2025.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant stated that allegations against a sitting judge must be handled through established institutional mechanisms and not determined in the public domain.
Justice Sandeep Mehta alleged that cases were abruptly withdrawn and transferred to Acting Chief Justice Sharma's bench without justifiable cause.
Justice Sandeep Mehta alleged that Acting Chief Justice Sharma organized a full court meeting on a working day to designate favored lawyers as senior advocates.
Justice Sandeep Mehta criticized a plan for a multi-storied guest house tower with nearly 100 rooms for the Rajasthan High Court as a waste of public funds.
Rajasthan High Court Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma is scheduled to retire on September 26.
Chief Justice of India Surya Kant confirmed he has requested a formal response from Acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma regarding the allegations.
Justice Sandeep Mehta urged the Supreme Court collegium to appoint a Chief Justice from another High Court to Rajasthan with immediate effect.
Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma was appointed a judge of the Rajasthan High Court in November 2016 and transferred to the Patna High Court in 2022.
In March 2023, the Supreme Court collegium headed by DY Chandrachud declined Justice Sharma's request to return to Rajasthan and transferred him to the Punjab and Haryana High Court.
In May 2025, the Supreme Court collegium recommended Justice Sharma's return to the Rajasthan High Court.
Justice Sandeep Mehta highlighted an advocate's complaint alleging Justice Sharma used his authority to appoint personal associates to permanent Lok Adalat positions in Jaipur and Ajmer.
